anatomy.flutter: Tooltip(label, child, delay, side, hidden) wraps child in a flutter.OverlayPortal whose overlay builds a CustomSingleChildLayout(_TooltipLayout) around TooltipContent(label, side) — a pill (StyledText on theme.foreground fill) plus a size-2.5 _ArrowPainter lane, matching the pill+arrow anatomy.
anatomy.web: TooltipProvider > Tooltip (TooltipPrimitive.Root) > TooltipTrigger > TooltipContent, which portals via TooltipPrimitive.Portal and renders the label plus a TooltipPrimitive.Arrow — the same trigger/content/arrow three-part anatomy Radix defines.

api.flutter: Tooltip's side parameter is a two-value TooltipSide{top,right} enum — the doc comment for it says explicitly 'top and right — the two the corpus asks for.'
api.web: Radix TooltipPrimitive.Content's side prop natively supports all four edges (top/right/bottom/left), reflected in tooltip.tsx's class list handling data-[side=bottom]:slide-in-from-top-2, data-[side=left]:slide-in-from-right-2, data-[side=right]:slide-in-from-left-2 and data-[side=top]:slide-in-from-bottom-2 all four.
api.note: RE-EXAMINED on review: the finding is correct and the direction is Flutter's. `TooltipSide` in tooltip.dart has only `top` and `right` because those are the two sides the Flutter corpus uses; the web exposes all four generically through Radix. The web is not short of anything here, so this is not a web gap — it is a Flutter shortfall, recorded as such so the Flutter side can pick it up. ORIGINAL: The Dart TooltipSide enum only has top and right members — there is no bottom or left case in the file at all, so a Flutter caller cannot position a tooltip below or to the left of its trigger the way any Radix TooltipContent can. This is scoped intentionally to what the current corpus uses (top is the default; right is SidebarMenuButton's collapsed-rail label) but it is a real capability the web exposes generically that the Flutter widget does not, and would need a third/fourth _TooltipLayout branch plus _ArrowPainter geometry to close.

states.flutter: Tooltip.delay defaults to MotionDurations.tooltipShowDelay, and the file's doc states 'TooltipProvider delayDuration={200} in app/layout.tsx, measured 232.5ms to first frame' as the value it is porting.
states.web: app/layout.tsx line 38 mounts '<TooltipProvider delayDuration={200}>{children}</TooltipProvider>' — the exact 200ms dwell the Flutter doc names, confirmed independent of tooltip.tsx's own component-level default of 0 (which is overridden by the app-wide provider).

disabled.flutter: Tooltip exposes a hidden: bool (not a disabled flag) — 'the trigger keeps its hover behaviour and nothing is rendered,' used when SidebarMenuButton wants the tooltip suppressed while the sidebar is expanded.
disabled.web: Radix TooltipPrimitive has no disabled prop of its own; a consumer simply does not render TooltipContent, or (as sidebar usage does) passes a hidden-equivalent flag through its own wrapper.
disabled.note: A tooltip is a passive label, not a control with an on/off affordance — hidden suppresses rendering while keeping the trigger's hover/tap plumbing live on both sides, which is not the same thing as a disabled dimension.

interaction.flutter: tooltip.dart implements a full touch path under 'USER-ORDERED MOBILE ADAPTATION': a Listener watches PointerDownEvent, a tap on the trigger opens/closes the tooltip with no dwell, a tap elsewhere (via a translucent barrier) closes it, and Tooltip.touchDwell (1.5s) auto-dismisses a tap-opened label so it can never be stranded on screen.
interaction.web: CLOSED: components/ui/tooltip.tsx's Tooltip now always drives Radix's Root as a controlled component (own uncontrolled state when the caller doesn't pass `open`), shared via a `TooltipOpenContext`; TooltipTrigger adds `onPointerDown`/`onPointerUp` handlers that, only when the interaction's `pointerType` was `"touch"`, `preventDefault()` and toggle that context's open state — leaving hover (`onPointerEnter`/`onPointerMove`, untouched, still Radix's own) and focus-visible-open (also untouched) exactly as they were for mouse and keyboard. An effect closes the tooltip on an outside `pointerdown` while a touch-opened tooltip is showing, since Radix's Content has no dismiss-on-outside-tap behavior of its own to reuse for this case.
interaction.note: CLOSED by this worker. Fixed in components/ui/tooltip.tsx — Tooltip and TooltipTrigger, per the web quote above. Measured live on /design-system/components/tooltip (dev server, http://localhost:3111) before the shared dev server later hit an unrelated Turbopack crash (a panic in app/globals.css's CSS pipeline, from concurrent work elsewhere in this repo, not this component): a synthetic `PointerEvent("pointerdown"/"pointerup", {pointerType: "touch"})` pair on the trigger opened the tooltip (`document.querySelector('[data-slot="tooltip-content"]')` went from absent to present). A first implementation toggled on the LIVE `ctx.open` read inside the `pointerup` handler and passed that same live check but failed a second-tap-closes test in jsdom: Radix's own Trigger already closes on any `pointerdown` while open (its own dismiss-on-next-interaction safety, in `onPointerDown: composeEventHandlers(props.onPointerDown, () => { if (context.open) context.onClose(); ... })` — @radix-ui/react-tooltip/dist/index.mjs), so by the time our `pointerup` ran, Radix had already flipped `ctx.open` to false and `!ctx.open` reopened the tooltip instead of leaving it closed — confirmed with a debug run that logged `data-state` through the gesture (`instant-open` -> `closed` on the second `pointerdown` alone, before our own `pointerup` even ran -> back to `instant-open` after it). Fixed by capturing `wasOpenRef` at `pointerdown` (before Radix's own handler can touch it) and deciding `pointerup`'s effect from that instead of the live value. `npx vitest run test/components/overlays/anchored.test.tsx` (jsdom, via `fireEvent.pointerDown`/`pointerUp` with `pointerType: "touch"`) pins open-on-tap, close-on-second-tap and close-on-outside-tap; hover and keyboard-focus paths are asserted unchanged in the same file. All three touch tests were confirmed to fail (RED) with the fix's `if` condition short-circuited to `false`, then confirmed to pass again once restored. `e2e/gaps-interaction.spec.ts` additionally exercises the same three paths in a real browser. Desktop hover/focus were not touched by this fix (untouched code paths, same className and Radix event handlers). Original finding kept below for the record. This is the one place the Flutter port is deliberately ahead of the web reference rather than behind it — the file's own doc frames it as a user order winning over the reference ('the reference is a mouse document, the order is a phone, and the order wins'), so there is nothing in this repository's web implementation for a touch user to reach an icon-only control's only name (a collapsed sidebar rail, a truncated AlertDialogAction). Recorded as a gap in the strict web-vs-Flutter sense (the web has no equivalent mechanism), but not a porting defect to fix — it is additional, intentionally unported-back capability.

semantics.flutter: tooltip.dart contains no Semantics node anywhere in the file — child is wrapped only in KeyedSubtree/MouseRegion/Listener, and the overlay's TooltipContent/_TooltipTransition/_TooltipLayout tree carries no semantic label, tooltip role, or aria-describedby-equivalent link back to the trigger.
semantics.web: Radix's TooltipTrigger/TooltipContent pair automatically wires aria-describedby from the trigger to the content's id, so a screen reader announces the tooltip's label when the trigger receives focus — a wiring Radix's primitive supplies for free.
semantics.note: RECLASSIFIED by this worker: gap -> flutter-behind. Re-reading the original finding, the divergence runs the wrong way for a `gap` verdict on THIS ledger (which measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, not the reverse, per check-audit.mjs's own verdict definitions) — the web already has the capability (Radix wires aria-describedby automatically, for free) and it is Flutter's tooltip.dart that has zero Semantics usage and no accessible-name path at all, as the note below (kept from the original finding) establishes directly from the file. There is nothing for the web to close here; if anything, this is Flutter's own gap against the web. Original finding, unedited: there is no accessible-naming path for this Flutter Tooltip at all — a screen-reader user focusing the wrapped trigger gets whatever semantics the trigger itself carries (e.g. a button's own label) but nothing that announces the tooltip's text, where the web trigger is described by its tooltip via aria-describedby automatically. This is a genuine parity gap, not merely unverified — the file has zero Semantics usage to point to.
